title: Rooms for rent that
fit the way you live
hero.body: Atrium is a six-floor residence for students and workers. Dorm beds from {from} a month up to two-bedroom flats, with every fee fixed and listed before you sign.

home.statement: Renting a room shouldn't mean surprise fees, vague contracts and a landlord who never picks up. Atrium puts every price on the table, fixes things fast, and lets you rent a fridge or a wardrobe only when you need one.
home.partnersNote: Students and staff of our partner universities and employers get the first month's service fee free.

title: Fees show up
after you've
signed
problems.text: Water by the person, power at a markup, a parking charge nobody mentioned. The rent was never the real price.

title: The room isn't
the one in
the photos
problems.text: Wide-angle pictures, no floor plan, no measurements. You find out how small it is on moving day.

title: Repairs wait
for weeks
on end
problems.text: A broken lock or a dead air conditioner becomes a chain of unanswered messages.

title: You pay for
furniture you
never use
problems.text: Furnished means whatever was left behind, priced into the rent whether you want it or not.

storySteps: Most listings show you a photo and a number. You only learn the size, the noise and the real monthly cost once you've moved in.
We drew every room in the building to scale, and fixed every fee before you see the rent.

useCases.title: Students
useCases.text: A dorm bed or single room ten minutes from campus, with a desk and fast Wi-Fi in every room.

useCases.title: Young professionals
useCases.text: A studio with its own kitchen, so you can cook after work and still save each month.

useCases.title: Shift workers
useCases.text: Quiet, blackout-curtained rooms and a security desk that's staffed all night.

useCases.title: Interns & trainees
useCases.text: Leases from three months, so a placement doesn't tie you into a year.

useCases.title: Couples
useCases.text: Studios and lofts that sleep two, with one bill for the both of you.

useCases.title: Friends sharing
useCases.text: Two-bedroom flats with lockable rooms and a shared kitchen and living room.

useCases.title: Remote workers
useCases.text: Top-floor lofts with space for a real desk, plus a co-working corner downstairs.

useCases.title: New to the city
useCases.text: Move in with one suitcase; rent the rest of what you need month by month.

dorm.name: Dorm bed
dorm.summary: A bunk in a four-bed room, with your own locker and desk.
dorm.text: The lowest rent in the building. Four residents share a bright room with two bunks, an ensuite bathroom and a desk each. Lockable storage and a reading light are yours alone.

single.name: Single room
single.summary: A private room for one, with a shower room of its own.
single.text: Your own door, your own key. A compact 12 m² room with a single bed, a wide desk under the window and a private shower room. The shared kitchen is two doors down.

studio.name: Studio
studio.summary: A room, kitchenette and bathroom: everything on one key.
studio.text: Room to live, not just sleep. A 20 m² studio with a double bed, a kitchenette with a two-ring hob, a fridge, and a bathroom. Fits one comfortably or two who like each other.

loft.name: Loft studio
loft.summary: A double-height studio with the bed up on a mezzanine.
loft.text: Top-floor ceilings, 4.6 m high. The bed sits on a mezzanine, which frees the whole floor below for a desk, a sofa and a proper kitchen. Each loft has a small balcony.

twobed.name: Two-bedroom
twobed.summary: Two bedrooms around a shared living room and kitchen.
twobed.text: Two lockable bedrooms off a shared living room with a full kitchen, a bathroom and a balcony. Rent it with a friend and pay less each than two studios.

faqs.q: Are the fixed fees really fixed?
faqs.a: Yes. Water, electricity, Wi-Fi, service and parking are flat monthly amounts set by your room type. They don't change with usage, and they can only go up once a year with 60 days' notice.
Nothing. Viewings are free, take about 20 minutes, and you can book one for any free or reserved room.

faqs.q: Can I rent furniture later, or return it?
faqs.a: Any time. Add a fridge, wardrobe or washing machine from the front desk or the resident app, and it's in your room the same day. Return it with a week's notice and it comes off your next bill.

faqs.q: Can I move to a different room?
faqs.a: Yes. Switching rooms inside Atrium is free; your lease carries over and your deposit moves with you. You pay the new room's rent from the day you move.
Anyone over 18 with ID. Most residents are students and people in their first jobs. Students and staff at our partner universities and employers get their first month's service fee free.

title: We're renters building
the home we always
wanted to rent
about.body: Atrium takes the guesswork out of renting a room: every room drawn to scale, every fee fixed before you sign, and furniture you rent only when you need it. Built by people who were tired of finding out the real price on moving day.
about.storyLead: An atrium is the open court at the heart of a building: the space everyone passes through, where the light comes in. That's how we wanted to run ours. Nothing hidden in a back office, every price out in the open, and a front desk that actually answers.
about.story: Atrium was started by two friends who had rented eleven rooms between them and never once known the real monthly cost before moving in. Fees appeared after signing, photos flattered the rooms, and repairs waited for weeks. So in 2024 they bought an empty office block in District 3 and rebuilt it as the place they wished they'd rented.
mission: Put every room on the plan, drawn to scale
List every fee before anyone signs
Let residents rent only the furniture they need
about.teamBody: We're a small team with backgrounds in architecture, property management and hospitality. What unites us: we've all been tenants, and we think renting a room should feel as clear as booking a hotel.
